$comment: Magenta's EUD catalogue. Addresses are StarCraft 1.16.1's, which Remastered's EUD layer maps; transcribed from Armoha's eud-book (MIT, see ATTRIBUTION.md) and the community's CUnit / dat layouts. `verified` means played and seen working in Remastered; nothing is verified until a map has been.

entries.name: Max hit points of a unit type

sentence.action: Set the max hit points of {unit} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The max hit points of {unit} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified: a marine made after the write had 100 HP (probe 8).

entries.name: Max shields of a unit type
Build time of a unit type
entries.note: Stored in frames at Normal speed: 15 per game second. Verified: a Barracks trained a marine in a second (probe 8).

entries.name: Mineral cost of a unit type
Gas cost of a unit type
Supply used by a unit type
entries.note: Stored in halves: a Zergling is 1.

entries.name: Supply provided by a unit type
entries.note: Verified: a depot made after the write provided 30 (probe 9).

entries.name: Sight range of a unit type
entries.note: In tiles, up to 11. Verified: a marine with sight 1 revealed only a tiny circle (probe 9). A beacon reveals around itself, so stand clear of one to see it.

entries.name: Target acquisition range of a unit type

sentence.action: Set the target acquisition range of {unit} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The target acquisition range of {unit} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: How far a unit looks for targets on its own. A write of 1 in probe 9 could not be read back; not yet seen working.

entries.name: Ground weapon of a unit type

sentence.action: Set the ground weapon of {unit} to {value}

entries.note: Verified: marines given the Arclite Shock Cannon fired it (probe 9). Units already on the map switch too.

entries.name: Air weapon of a unit type

sentence.action: Set the air weapon of {unit} to {value}

entries.note: Verified: marines with no air weapon ignored an overlord (probe 9).

entries.name: Speed of a unit type
entries.source: flingy.dat movement control, top speed, acceleration, halt distance (DatEdit's layout)
entries.note: Four records: the unit's flingy is switched to table control and given this top speed, with acceleration and stopping distance to match. Units made after this move at the new speed; the ones already on the map keep theirs. A Marine walks at 4, a Vulture at 6.7. Hero units that share a type's flingy change with it.

entries.name: Name of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat map string index (Remastered's unit names from the map's strings)
entries.note: The name comes from one of the map's strings, shown wherever the unit's name appears; the one type only. Remastered only.

entries.name: Size of a unit type
entries.note: What concussive and explosive damage scale by: small takes full concussive damage and half explosive, large the other way round. Verified: a vulture took 5 off a large marine (probe 9).

entries.name: Looks of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat graphics (the flingy a unit type draws through)
entries.note: Units made after this draw as the other type; the ones already on the map keep their look. Stats, size and weapons stay the type's own.

entries.name: Detector flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag. Units of the type see cloaked and burrowed units in their sight range.

entries.name: Permanent cloak flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag: units made after this have it; the ones already on the map keep what they were made with.

entries.name: Cloak ability flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag, bit 9. Verified as a write and read (probe 9); what the game does with it for a type that never had it was not checked — the flag alone gives no button.

entries.name: Burrow ability flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag, bit 20. Verified as a write and read (probe 9); what the game does with it for a type that never had it was not checked — the flag alone gives no button.

entries.name: Regeneration flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag. Verified on marines already on the map: their hit points climbed at once (probe 8).

entries.name: Invincible flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag: units made after this cannot be hurt; the ones already on the map keep what they were made with (probe 8).

entries.name: Hero flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag, bit 6. Verified as a write and read (probe 9); what the game does with it for a type that never had it was not checked — the flag alone gives no button.

entries.name: Organic flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag. Verified: a medic healed a vulture flagged organic (probe 9), one already on the map.

entries.name: Mechanical flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag. Verified: an SCV could repair a marine flagged mechanical (probe 9), one already on the map.

entries.name: Robotic flag of a unit type
entries.source: units.dat special ability flags (DatEdit's bit order)
entries.note: A units.dat flag, bit 14. Verified as a write and read (probe 9); what the game does with it for a type that never had it was not checked — the flag alone gives no button.

entries.name: Damage bonus per upgrade of a weapon

sentence.action: Set the damage bonus per upgrade of {weapon} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The damage bonus per upgrade of {weapon} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Extra damage per upgrade level. Verified (probe 9).

entries.name: Cooldown of a weapon
entries.note: In frames. Verified (probe 9).

entries.name: Damage factor of a weapon
entries.note: Hits per attack. Verified (probe 9).

entries.name: Range of a weapon
entries.note: In pixels, 32 a tile. Verified: marines shot from farther (probe 8).

entries.name: Minimum range of a weapon
entries.note: In pixels, 32 a tile. Verified: marines could not shoot a zergling up close (probe 9).

entries.name: Mineral cost of an upgrade
entries.note: The first level's cost; each further level adds the upgrade's own factor to it.

entries.name: Gas cost of an upgrade
entries.note: The first level's cost; each further level adds the upgrade's own factor to it.

entries.name: Research time of an upgrade
entries.note: The first level's time, stored in frames at Normal speed: 15 per game second. Each further level adds the upgrade's own factor.

entries.name: Maximum level of an upgrade
entries.note: How many times the upgrade can be researched. Writing it did nothing in Remastered (probe 8: Infantry Armor still stopped at 3), so it is a read only.

entries.name: Research time of a technology
entries.note: Stored in frames at Normal speed: 15 per game second.

entries.name: Energy cost of a technology
entries.note: What a cast of the spell takes. Verified: lockdown at 10 energy (probe 8).

entries.name: Minerals of a player
entries.note: The same number Set Resources changes, without the resource counter's sound.

entries.name: Gas of a player
entries.note: Verified: +500 gas (probe 8).

entries.name: Upgrade level of a player
entries.source: current upgrade level, the 46 original upgrades (eud-book)
entries.note: Verified: Infantry Weapons set to 3 showed on the marines (probe 8).

entries.name: Technology researched by a player
entries.note: Verified: Lockdown and Personnel Cloaking researched at the start of probe 8, and the ghost could cast.

entries.name: Alliance of a player toward another

sentence.action: Set the stance of {player} toward {other} to {value}

entries.note: As a condition this reads what Set Alliance Status wrote; the game has no native way to test it. Verified both ways in probe 9. The catalogue had this at 0x58D6F8 until 2026-09-14, which is the game clock.

entries.name: Shared vision between players
entries.note: Player 2's row with Player 1's bit on lets Player 1 see what Player 2 sees: the row is whose sight is shared, the bit who receives it (probe 9).

entries.name: Colour of a player
entries.source: unit colour table 0x581D76 and minimap colour table 0x581DD6 (eud-book)
entries.note: Two records: the palette entry the player's units are drawn in, and the one the minimap uses. Takes effect at once, for every unit of the player.

entries.name: Supply provided to a player
entries.note: The right-hand number of the top bar, before the cap. The game recounts it when a depot, overlord or pylon is made or lost, so set it every frame to hold a value. Each race has its own table; a player's is the one for the race they play.

entries.name: Supply used by a player
entries.note: The left-hand number of the top bar. The game recounts it when a unit is made or dies. Each race has its own table; a player's is the one for the race they play. Verified as a read (probe 9).

entries.name: Supply cap of a player
entries.note: What the provided supply is capped at, 200 in a normal game. Each race has its own table; a player's is the one for the race they play.

entries.name: Slot of a player
entries.note: What the slot holds once the game has started: a human, a computer, or nothing. Verified: read at the start of probe 9.

entries.name: Race of a player
entries.note: The race the player picked, once the game has started. Verified: read at the start of probe 9.

entries.name: Whether a player has left
entries.note: Set once a human leaves. Not yet seen working in Remastered.

entries.name: Game speed
entries.note: Writing it did nothing in Remastered (probe 5, 2026-09-14), so it is a read only: what the speed setting is.

entries.name: Trigger timer
entries.note: Set to 0 every cycle by the every-frame switch; every probe map runs on it.

entries.name: Local player

sentence.condition: The player at this computer is {value}

entries.note: Differs per computer: what follows runs for that player's screen only, so keep it to text, sounds and the view.

entries.name: Mouse X on screen

sentence.condition: The mouse's X on screen is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Local to each computer, like the local player.

entries.name: Mouse Y on screen

sentence.condition: The mouse's Y on screen is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Local to each computer, like the local player.

entries.name: Screen X on the map

sentence.condition: The screen's left edge on the map is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Local to each computer. Center View moves it natively.

entries.name: Screen Y on the map

sentence.condition: The screen's top edge on the map is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Local to each computer. Center View moves it natively.

entries.name: Keyboard key state
entries.note: Local to each computer. Needs triggers running every frame to catch a press. Verified in Remastered 2026-09-12: the press reads as 1 for a frame and the key reads 0 again at once, even while held; 2 and 3 never appeared.

entries.name: Frames the game has run
entries.note: About 24 a second at Fastest, 15 at Normal. Verified: a line at 10 s (probe 8).

entries.name: Seconds on the game clock
entries.note: The seconds the in-game clock shows. The earlier entry at 0x58D6F4 (the countdown timer) never fired; this one is the next dword. Verified: a line at 15 s (probe 8).

entries.name: Hit points of a placed unit

sentence.action: Set the hit points of placed unit {index} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The hit points of placed unit {index} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified in Remastered 2026-09-12. Slots: the first placed unit is slot 0 and later ones count down from 1699 (verified in Remastered 2026-09-12); the chip picks a unit on the map and works the slot out. Start locations take no slot; nor does a unit of a human player who is not in the game (it is removed at load), so slots after one shift by one when that player is missing.

entries.name: Shields of a placed unit

sentence.action: Set the shields of placed unit {index} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The shields of placed unit {index} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified: a placed Zealot set to 0 shields (probe 8).

entries.name: Energy of a placed unit

sentence.action: Set the energy of placed unit {index} {mod} {value}
sentence.condition: The energy of placed unit {index} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified (probe 8). A value past the unit's maximum shows for a frame and is clamped back by the game, so 250 on a Ghost reads 200/200.

entries.name: Owner of a placed unit

sentence.action: Set the owner of placed unit {index} to {value}
sentence.condition: The owner of placed unit {index} is {value}

entries.note: Changes the owner byte only: the unit turns hostile or friendly at once, but keeps its old colour (that lives on its sprite) and its selection and control groups. Give Units is the clean way. Verified in Remastered 2026-09-12. Slots: the first placed unit is slot 0 and later ones count down from 1699 (verified in Remastered 2026-09-12); the chip picks a unit on the map and works the slot out. Start locations take no slot; nor does a unit of a human player who is not in the game (it is removed at load), so slots after one shift by one when that player is missing.

entries.name: Type of a placed unit
entries.note: Slot order as for hit points: not simply map order, being probed. Slots: the first placed unit is slot 0 and later ones count down from 1699 (verified in Remastered 2026-09-12); the chip picks a unit on the map and works the slot out. Start locations take no slot; nor does a unit of a human player who is not in the game (it is removed at load), so slots after one shift by one when that player is missing.

entries.name: X position of a placed unit

sentence.condition: The X of placed unit {index} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified (probe 9).

entries.name: Y position of a placed unit

sentence.condition: The Y of placed unit {index} is {cmp} {value}

entries.note: Verified (probe 9).

sentence.action: Set invincibility of placed unit {index} to {value}

entries.name: Hallucination flag of a placed unit

sentence.action: Set the hallucination flag of placed unit {index} to {value}
sentence.condition: The hallucination flag of placed unit {index} is {value}

entries.source: CUnit statusFlags at +0xDC, bit 30 (community CUnit layout)
entries.note: Verified as a write (probe 9): the unit is labelled a hallucination and takes hallucination damage, but the tint and the timed death come from a real cast, not this bit.

entries.name: Cloak state of a placed unit

sentence.condition: The cloak of placed unit {index} is {value}

entries.source: CUnit statusFlags at +0xDC, bit 9 (community CUnit layout)
entries.note: Verified: read while a ghost was cloaked (probe 9).
